blocks.heading: Get a requirement-level review
blocks.lead: The review looks at two things: how easily your resume can be read, and how well it answers this job.

items.title: Parsing and readability
items.text: Formats, headings and layout that some systems read poorly, with a plain-text alternative.

items.title: Job-specific evidence gaps
items.text: Requirements from the job that your resume does not yet show, checked against your verified profile.

blocks.heading: Fix issues without keyword stuffing
blocks.lead: Every issue has a reason and a fix. Fixes reword facts you already have; they never add new ones.
blocks.frameLabel: Resume check · Senior Product Manager, Payments

items.why: Some parsers read “2019–21” and “Mar 2021” differently and can misplace roles.
items.fix: Use one format for every role, for example “Mar 2019 – Jun 2021”.

items.issue: Skills appear only inside a table
items.why: Some applicant tracking systems skip table content when they extract text.
items.fix: Add a plain-text Skills section below the summary.

items.issue: The job’s term “stakeholder management” is missing
items.why: The job lists it twice. Your profile describes the same work as “cross-team planning”.
items.fix: Use the job’s wording where it describes a fact already in your profile.

blocks.heading: What an ATS score can and cannot tell you
blocks.lead: A score is one signal about readability and keyword coverage. It is not a verdict from any employer’s system.

items.title: It cannot guarantee a pass
items.text: Employers configure their systems differently, and no outside tool can confirm how yours will read a resume.

items.title: It does not predict interviews
items.text: A resume that reads well helps people find your evidence. Hiring decisions depend on much more.

items.title: Different tools disagree
items.text: Two checkers can score the same resume differently. Focus on the issues and reasons, not on one number.

items.title: It should not push you to add keywords
items.text: Repeating terms without matching experience hurts readability and can mislead the reader.

faqs.a: The review focuses on issues, reasons and fixes rather than on one number. Any score shown is labeled with what it does and does not mean.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a checker and an optimizer?
faqs.a: A checker diagnoses. An optimizer also proposes fixes you can review, edit or reject. This page describes the second.
